title: resolve-hourly-window-skew-from-rate-limit-retries-leading-to-proration-misallocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Customers are seeing proration differences and occasional negative invoice line items when late meter events arrive after rate-limit retries. Investigation shows our hourly export anchoring and dedupe semantics allow some retried events to be bucketed into the previous hour (hour-window skew), which then triggers proration adjustments on the subsequent invoice export. This ticket stabilizes the hourly export boundary logic, makes export aggregation idempotent across retry storms, and adjusts proration rounding to avoid negative line generation.

Background/details:
- Symptoms: reduced invoice accuracy (small negative line items, flickering proration values) correlated with high rate-limit retry windows (observed during quota bursts and SDK retry storms).
- Root cause (summary): 1) retried meter events retain the original request_id but sometimes have an altered ingestion timestamp due to retries hitting different ingestion nodes; 2) exporter currently anchors hourly buckets using the event ingestion timestamp with UTC-hour boundaries; when a retry crosses the hour boundary it can be counted into the previous hour while the primary accounted usage stayed in the later hour -> leads to duplicate or moved usage in exports. 3) The proration logic distributes fractional cents deterministically, but negative deltas can appear when late corrections are applied without a stable ordering.
- Impact: medium on invoice accuracy (affects small subset of customers during high retry periods), higher on accounting exports and reconciler diffs (noise causes manual intervention).

What we'll do in this ticket:
1) Make exporter bucketization deterministic and resilient to retries: switch to using the event's original client_timestamp (when present) as the primary bucketing key; fall back to ingestion_timestamp only when client_timestamp missing. Normalize to ISO hour boundaries with half-open intervals [H, H+1). This reduces cross-hour mis-bucketing from retries.
2) Add a persistent dedupe fingerprint to meter events: fingerprint := sha256(customer_id || meter_name || client_timestamp || request_id || retry_seq). Persist fingerprint in the inline usage ledger and use it during export aggregation to ensure idempotency across retries and replayed events.
3) Modify the export reconciler to perform a deterministic merge when late events are applied: calculate delta lines instead of rewriting entire invoice lines when export window changed; ensure negative deltas are clamped and traced with audit tags to avoid producing opaque negative line items.
4) Adjust proration rounding algorithm: when distributing fractional cents across split invoice lines, use a stable 'round toward oldest line' policy and persist the remainder token so subsequent corrections are distributable without flipping signs.
5) Add observability and a dry-run mode for 2 weeks: Reconciler will emit a side-by-side export diff metric (current vs. proposed) per-customer and an alert for >0.1% of customers with changed invoice amounts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Exports generated with dry-run flag enabled produce zero negative line items for a representative 30-day backfill of high-retry customers.
- Diffs between current and proposed export logic are below threshold for normal traffic (<0.1% customers with >$1 delta) and actionable spikes have diagnostics.
- Reconciler idempotency test (simulated retry storms) shows 100% dedupe (no duplicated usage counts) across 10k synthetic events.
- No downstream schema changes required for Stripe/NetSuite exports; changes are additive (audit tags, fingerprint fields) and backward compatible.
tasks: add client_timestamp-first bucketing with half-open hour intervals
implement and persist dedupe fingerprint in usage ledger
update export reconciler to emit delta-only invoice changes and clamp negative deltas
change proration rounding to 'round to oldest' and persist remainder token
add metric/reporting for side-by-side dry-run diffs and a dashboard
run 2-week dry-run against staging + a selected cohort in prod (feature flag)
postmortem & runbook updates for billing ops
acceptance_criteria: No negative invoice line items produced in dry-run for 30-day high-retry backfill
Dedupe test shows no duplicated usage for retry storm simulation
Side-by-side diff metric below 0.1% customers exceeding $1 delta over baseline
All changes behind feature flag with clear rollback path
risks: Changing bucketing key may surface previously-hidden late-arrival corrections leading to short-term diff churn
If client_timestamp is spoofed or missing, we must ensure fallback to ingestion_timestamp doesn't reintroduce skew
Persisted fingerprint increases storage index size — need to monitor ledger table growth and GC policy
rollout_plan: Implement logic behind feature flag and tests (unit + integration)
Deploy to staging and run end-to-end backfill tests against synthetic high-retry dataset
Enable dry-run in prod for 5% of customers (billing cohort) for 2 weeks, collect diffs and alerts
If metrics stable, expand to 50% for one week, then full enablement and remove dry-run metrics after 30 days
If regressions > threshold, disable flag and revert via documented rollback PR
monitoring: alerts: PagerDuty if >0.5% customers experiencing >$5 delta in a 24h window
